speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the Ministry will consider extending the maximum age of vocational licences for driving such as the Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence and the Private Hire Car Driver's Vocational Licence, should the driver be certified to be medically fit to drive a vehicle by a medical professional; and (b) if this is not possible, in what circumstances will the Ministry consider this on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: As taxi and private hire car (PHC) drivers spend a significant amount of time on the road and are responsible for the safety of commuters and other road users, it is important to ensure that they are fit to drive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: SMA found the accident rate of older vocational drivers to be higher than that of younger vocational drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA will continue to monitor the sector and review the statutory age limit periodically, to ensure an appropriate balance between safety and allowing older drivers to remain in their vocation.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: From the National Taxi Association members' data, the average age of our members has increased by about five years from 10 years ago.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our members have expressed their desire to continue driving past the age of 75 as they feel they are still in good health and have mental alertness.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In addition, the past two COVID-19 years have been very tough on our drivers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And many of them have had their nest eggs wiped out, hence the appeal to continue driving past the retirement age.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Should our drivers pass an annual medical examination, complete with eye and hearing test, will the LTA consider a restricted licence for a senior driver driving, for example, limited hours or limited routes?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But, as I have noted, we will continue to monitor the sector as we have been doing and we will review the statutory age limit periodically, making sure that we have a balance between safety as well as allowing the older drivers to remain in the vocation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Taiwan is another jurisdiction that has got a statutory age limit on their taxi drivers and their current statutory age limit is 70 years – so we are already above their current age limit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, as I have said, we will continue to monitor and review this periodically.
